extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from MPEP sections concerning reissue applications, reexamination proceedings, national stage/PCT practice, protests, petitions, fees, and related prosecution/task handling. Focused on examiner and practitioner obligations and timing/fee/transmittal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadened-claim presentation in reissue after two-year period
rubrics_metrics.description: A broadened claim may be presented in a reissue application after the two year period even though the broadened claim presented after the two years is different than the broadened claim presented within the two year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue practice permits presentation of a broadened claim after the two-year window; examiners/practitioners should be aware that a later broadened claim need not be identical to one presented earlier within the two-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent requirement for deleting inventor in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion added regarding when an inventor whose name is to be deleted in a reissue application must consent to the filing of the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should determine and document whether a named inventor's consent is required to delete their name in a reissue filing and follow the MPEP guidance on when consent is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration noncompliance handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reissue oath/declaration fails to comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.63, form paragraph 14.01.05 should be used in conjunction with the content of form paragraphs 6.05 through 6.05.02, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the updated forms PTO/SB/51 and PTO/SB/52 and apply form paragraph 14.01.05 with the indicated form paragraphs to address deficient reissue oaths/declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical surrender of original patent eliminated
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective October 21, 2004, the requirement for physical surrender of the original letters patent in a reissue application has been eliminated; surrender of the original patent is automatic upon the grant of the reissue patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should no longer require or check for physical surrender; related obsolete forms (e.g., PTO/SB/55) have been deleted and examiner instructions referencing physical surrender were removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to IFW reissue application file history
rubrics_metrics.description: The general public can view the entire content of an IFW reissue application file history by way of Public PAIR via the USPTO Internet site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and practitioners should assume IFW reissue file contents are publicly accessible on Public PAIR and act accordingly when filing sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.182 based on litigation must identify specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the basis for a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 is ongoing litigation, the petition must clearly identify the litigation and detail the specifics of the litigation that call for prompt action on the reissue application prior to the expiration of the 2-month delay period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions premised on litigation should include clear identification and specifics (e.g., case name, court, issues, timing) to justify expedited processing before the statutory delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest timing and treatment under 37 CFR 1.291
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest under 37 CFR 1.291 may be filed throughout the pendency of a reissue application. Except where accompanied by written consent of the applicant, a protest under 37 CFR 1.291(a) must be submitted prior to the date the application was published under 37 CFR 1.211. If prosecution is closed or a final rejection issued, a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with the required fee for entry may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests must meet timing rules to be considered during prosecution; if late (post-publication) and without consent, they may be barred. For closed prosecution, entry of a late protest requires a petition and fee. Early filing is important for ‘reissue litigation’ protests to be considered at first action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on cumulative prior art submissions by same real party
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective November 22, 2004, 37 CFR 1.291(c) was amended to no longer permit the submission of additional (cumulative) prior art by the same real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party protestors cannot repeatedly submit the same (cumulative) prior art; subsequent submissions by the same real party are restricted by the amended rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination not stayed by litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte reexamination proceeding will not be stayed where there is litigation; therefore, where a reissue application has been merged with an ex parte reexamination proceeding, the merged proceeding will not be stayed where there is litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merging reissue and ex parte reexamination does not cause a stay due to litigation; examiners and practitioners should proceed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW processing references and considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple sections were revised to add discussion regarding IFW (Image File Wrapper) processing and to indicate that the public may view IFW file histories via Public PAIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IFW processes for electronic file handling; be aware that IFW files are publicly accessible and that specific IFW procedures exist for entry of amendments and clerical handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notification when multiple reissue/reexam proceedings pending
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner becomes aware that multiple reissue applications are pending for the same patent, and an ex parte or inter partes reexamination proceeding is pending for the same patent, the examiner should inform the TC SPRE immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely inform the TC SPRE to coordinate potential merges or other cross-file processing; reference MPEP § 2285 and § 2686.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference-provocation requirement under 37 CFR 41.202(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 41.202(c), an examiner may require a reissue applicant to add a claim to provoke an interference, unless the reissue applicant cannot present the added claim to provoke an interference based on the provisions of the reissue statute and rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue applicants may be required to add claims for interference purposes; if unable to present such claims under statutory/rule constraints, they are not required to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application filing while original patent in interference
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application is filed while the original patent is in an interference proceeding, the reissue applicant must promptly notify the Board of the filing of the reissue application within 20 days from the filing date of the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification (within 20 days) to the Board is required to coordinate interference and reissue processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-claim rule across divisional reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The same patent claim cannot be presented for examination in more than one of the divisional reissue applications, as a pending claim, in either its original or amended versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid presenting identical pending claims across divisional reissue files; coordinate claim placement to prevent duplicate pending claim examination across divisional reissues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design reissue fee requirements (post-Dec 8, 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: For design reissue applications filed on or after December 8, 2004, a search fee and an examination fee are also required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include applicable search and examination fees with design reissue filings made on/after the effective date to avoid processing delays or deficiency notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of assignee and inventor names; 119/120 benefits corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: New sections were added directed to correction of assignees' names, correction of inventors' names, and correction of 35 U.S.C. 119 and 120 benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the new, separate procedures set out in the updated MPEP subsections for correcting assignee names, inventor names, and claiming 119/120 benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered practitioner cannot sign a disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 is not permitted to sign a disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimers must be signed by the correct party (applicant/owner) and not by a representative under 1.34; practitioners should ensure proper signature compliance and use updated forms PTO/SB/43, PTO/SB/25, PTO/SB/26 as revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific reference to parent application in continuation/CIP
rubrics_metrics.description: In a continuation or continuation-in-part application, a specific reference to the parent application must be included in an application data sheet or in the first sentence(s) of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the required reference to the parent (35 U.S.C. 120/37 CFR 1.78(a)(2)(iii)) to ensure proper benefit claim; to expedite examination, certify at filing that the international application has not been withdrawn when claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage commencement and late-submission handling (35 U.S.C. 371)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of an express request for early processing under 35 U.S.C. 371(f) and compliance with the conditions provided therein, the U.S. national stage will commence upon expiration of 30 months from the priority date. If the basic national fee paid and copy received by 30 months but other required items (oath/declaration, translation, search/exam fees, application size fee) are missing, the Office will send a notice and provide a period to correct as set in 37 CFR 1.495(c). Processing fees and surcharges (per 37 CFR 1.492) apply for late acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required items are filed by the commencement date or file an express early-processing request; otherwise expect notices and additional processing fees/surcharges for late submissions (e.g., translation acceptance fee under 1.492(i), surcharge under 1.492(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 19 amendments and English translations timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Article 19 amendment(s) and the English translation of the amendment(s) must be received by the Office by the date of commencement of the national stage; otherwise, the amendment(s) will be considered canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit Article 19 amendments and English translations by the national stage commencement date to avoid cancellation; delayed submissions may not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations of annexes for national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: If annexes are in a foreign language, a proper translation of the annexes must be furnished not later than the expiration of 30 months from the priority date, unless a period has been set pursuant to 37 CFR 1.495(c), in which case translations accompanied by the processing fee under 1.492(f) may be submitted within that later period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File translations of annexes timely or secure a period under 1.495(c) and include processing fees when filing translations late per the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor name discrepancies: petition vs. notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there has been no change of inventorship but the name differs (e.g., due to marriage), a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 will be required to accept the oath/declaration with the changed name. However, typographical or transliteration errors do not require a petition and may be corrected by simply notifying the Office; a new oath or declaration is not required to correct such errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between substantive name changes (require petition) and typographical/transliteration errors (notify Office; no petition/new oath needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention election and rejoinder guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner determines that the claims lack unity of invention and requires election of a single invention, when all of the claims drawn to the elected invention are allowable, the claims directed to the nonelected invention(s) should be considered for rejoinder following the guidance set forth in MPEP § 821.04(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 821.04(b) for rejoinder procedures when elected claims become allowable and consider rejoinder of nonelected claims accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of reexamination and effect of terminated reexamination prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: When the prosecution of a reexamination proceeding is terminated, a reexamination certificate is issued which indicates the status of all claims following the reexamination. Unless prosecution is reopened by the Director, the reexamination proceeding is concluded by the issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that reexamination termination results in a certificate describing claim status; reopening requires Director action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination fees: scope and excess-claim fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees for a reexamination proceeding include the fees for the request, for addition of claims, for a request for an extension of time, for any appeal, brief, and oral hearing. No fee is required for the issuance of a reexamination certificate. If an amendment is submitted to add claims to the patent being reexamined, excess claims fees may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing amendments that add claims or requesting extensions or appeals in reexamination, assess and pay applicable fees (including excess claims fees) to avoid defects; issuance of the reexamination certificate itself carries no fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of amended addresses and forms on submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to reflect amendments to 37 CFR 1.33. The addresses for submitting changes of correspondence address or power of attorney and for reexamination requests and correspondence have been updated and related forms (e.g., PTO/SB/82, PTO/SB/83) updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the updated addresses and updated forms for correspondence, reexamination requests, and power-of-attorney filings to ensure proper routing and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination e-File and electronic processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion and instructions regarding reexamination e-File and entry of amendments for IFW reexamination files have been added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reexamination e-File and IFW procedures according to updated MPEP guidance; electronic entry of amendments follows new instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-or-subsequent reexamination requests raising SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: If a second or subsequent request for reexamination is filed while a first ex parte reexamination is pending, the second or subsequent request for reexamination may raise a substantial new question of patentability with respect to any new or amended claim which has been proposed in the first (or prior) pending reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent reexamination requests can rely on new/amended claims in earlier pending reexam proceedings to establish a substantial new question; examiners and CRU should consider such interactions when deciding entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of prior art copies to patent owner and requester
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the request for reexamination was filed by a third party, copies of any prior art documents not already supplied by or to the patent owner or requester will be provided to the patent owner and the requester. Clerical staff should make 2 copies of the prior art documents not already supplied, one for the patent owner and one for the 3rd party requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper distribution of prior art copies to both patent owner and third-party requester to enable response and comment; update file records accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection of reexamination files via Public PAIR
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination files are open to inspection by the general public by way of the Public PAIR via the USPTO Internet site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners and patent owners should assume reexamination file contents are publicly accessible and manage confidential information appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU denial mailing and jurisdiction retention
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision denying the request for reexamination is mailed by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) and jurisdiction over the reexamination is retained by the CRU to await any petition seeking review of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When CRU denies entry, it will mail the decision and retain jurisdiction pending any petition; practitioners should timely file petitions if contesting denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for third-party comments when excess claims fee unpaid
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a failure to pay an excess claims fee by the patent owner, the third party requester does not have the new claim 'package' to comment on. Thus, the third party requester comments may be filed within 30 days from the date of service of the patent owner’s response correcting the excess claims fee deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an excess claims fee deficiency prevents third-party access to amended claims, third parties get a 30-day window after service of a correcting response to file comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of defective paper and petitions for return
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a paper is to be returned based on subsection II and the paper is not accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 or 1.183, the TC Director will return the paper. Where a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 or 1.183 has been filed, the reexamination proceeding should be forwarded to OPLA for a decision on the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers judged defective will be returned unless accompanied by the appropriate petition; if petitioned, forward to OPLA for adjudication instead of immediate return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after appeal and timing of automatic extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission after appeal (e.g., amendment filed under 37 CFR 41.33) does not place the reexamination proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate, the period for filing an appeal brief continues to run (i.e., 2 months from the date of filing the notice of appeal – 37 CFR 41.37(a)(1)) until an appeal brief or an amendment that places the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate is filed. Also, the automatic one-month extension of time granted as a result of a timely first response to a final rejection does not apply once the Notice of Appeal has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that after filing a notice of appeal, automatic timing rules change and amendments after appeal are governed by 37 CFR 41.33/41.63; filing an amendment that does not place the case in condition for certificate does not stop the appeal brief deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination sample/example guidance (grant vs denial)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP examples illustrate a grant of an ex parte reexamination request (first example) and a denial of an ex parte reexamination request (second example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the MPEP examples to understand factual distinctions that lead to grant versus denial of ex parte reexamination requests.
